feedback.end: On the 21st of July 1796, Burns died. He was only 37 years old.

atoms.b: Five years after Burns died, his ((++friends puppies)) gathered to celebrate his life. During this meeting, they read his ((++poems pictures)) aloud and ate a special meal.
Now, every year on ((++Burns’ Daniel’s)) birthday, the 25th of January, people continue this tradition. It is called Burns Night.
atoms.sound: Now, every year on Burns’s birthday, the 25th of January, people continue this tradition. It is called Burns Night.

instruction.text: Drag the foods to the correct places on the table.

feedback.finish: On Burns Night, people eat mashed potatoes, called tatties, mashed turnips, called neeps, and haggis. Haggis is a traditional Scottish food made from sheep’s organs, oats and spices.

end.text: On Burns Night, people also read Burns’ poems aloud. One tradition is to perform his poem Address to a Haggis, which explains the dish’s importance.
end.sound: On Burns Night, people also reed Burns’s poems aloud. One tradition is to perform his poem 'Address to a Haggis', which explains the dish’s importance.

atoms.a: What else do you think people do on Burns night?

instruction.text: As well as reading Burns’ poems, people also say The Selkirk Grace before dinner. What language is this written in?
instruction.sound: As well as reading Burns’s poems, people also say the Selkirk Grace before dinner. What language is this written in?

atoms.a: Some hay meat, and canna eat, and some wud eat that want it. But wee hay meat, and we can eat, and say the lord be thank-it.

feedback.finish: Even though Burns did not write The Selkirk Grace, it is another example of Scots writing being used to show national pride.

atoms.b: Although some people think that ((++Burns Ben)) wrote The Selkirk Grace, he actually just recited it at a dinner party.
The prayer had existed for around ((++100 1)) years before Burns but, as Burns was famous, he made it more popular.

atoms.a: Why is Burns still important today?

feedback.end: As he wrote in Scots and talked a lot about Scottish culture, Burns is viewed by many as the greatest Scottish writer of all time.
